paras: The killing of Lee Moore was the fatal shooting of a Black man by two officers at Junction City, Arkansas, in August 1900, while they were arresting him on a warrant. A coroner's jury exonerated the officers, and the story circulated as a short item in Arkansas state-news columns and, briefly, in Texas.

No report gives the date of the shooting, but the earliest notice appeared in the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic on August 23, 1900. According to the brief that ran under the heading "Killed by Officers," the officers had served a warrant of arrest on Moore in his yard when he began cursing them, ran into his house and came out with a pistol. As he started to raise the weapon, the same account said, a bullet from one of the officers' pistols pierced his heart and he fell dead. None of the reports states what charge the warrant carried.
The Pine Bluff paper named the officers as J. W. Marcus and O. H. Burke and reported that a coroner's jury had exonerated them. No report of any further inquiry or proceeding appears in the coverage.

Only white newspapers carried the killing, and all of them told it from the officers' side. The Pine Bluff Daily Graphic gave it a single sentence, describing Moore as "colored" and saying he was shot "while resisting arrest." The fuller "Killed by Officers" brief, which presented the officers' version as fact without naming a source, appeared in the Forrest City Times on August 24. Within a week the same text ran word for word in the Van Buren Press, the Conway Log Cabin, the Malvern Times-Journal and the De Queen Bee, each time among other Arkansas news items.
Outside Arkansas, the Shiner Gazette in Texas reduced the story to one line in its "Events of Everywhere" column on September 5. No account of the killing was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Killing of Lee Moore
bases: Moore was shot dead by officers serving a warrant of arrest on him, with no crowd or mob reported (A1, A2).

Two differently worded Arkansas reports agree that officers shot and killed Lee Moore at Junction City while arresting him (A1, A2), though both give only the officers' side and may trace to the same local source.
